effect: Every island clear writes a CONTINUE password to the screen map, never shown

effect: Game A's round clock never counts down
note: Game Genie: $00:3C87 RET NZ (C0) -> RET (C9) in the Game A clock routine ($00:3C7D: DEC frame counter $C0EE, then DEC time $C0EF); it now always returns before the time byte is decremented. Same bytes at the same address in Bomber Boy. BizHawk: US and JP: new game, Hevol, round start; $C0EF sampled every 120 frames: without 199,198,197,196,195... (stops when the player dies); with the code 200 x12. GameShark (held every frame): Holds $C0EF at 200: US and JP stayed 200 for 1,440 frames (one 199 blip in US between writes). Not checked: the round-end TIME tally counts $C0EF down, so a held value may stall it. Mesen 2 (Dynablaster, and Bomberman Collection through its menu; cheat engine): same bytes at $00:3C87; the Game A round clock stayed 200 for 1,440 frames with the code (199 -> 189 without); GameShark 01C8EFC0 also held 200 on both.

effect: The Panel Shop sells the panels that are still locked (shown as ?) before their island is cleared, and shows their name and price

The first code alone already lets you buy; the second only reveals the name and price. BizHawk: US and JP: new game (islands 0, 100 gold), shop BUY, cursor to the 4th icon (SPEED UP, a ? icon), A. Without: gold stays 100, PRICE/EFFECT = ???. With both: PRICE 20 / EFFECT SPEED UP, gold 100 -> 80, YOUR PANELS 8 -> 9. With only 21E-D4D-C41: still ??? but gold 100 -> 80. Mesen 2 (Dynablaster, and Bomberman Collection through its menu; cheat engine): same bytes at $00:2ED4 / $00:2E38; buying the 4th (locked) panel took gold 100 -> 80 with both codes and with 21E-D4D-C41 alone, 100 -> 100 without.

effect: Game B never takes a life away when you die
note: Game Genie: $02:417C DEC A (3D) -> AND A (A7) in the death path ($02:4176: LDH A,($FF94); game over if 0; DEC; store), so $FF94 is stored back unchanged. BizHawk: US and JP: same 4,000-frame bot run in Game B; without the code $FF94 went 2 -> 1 -> 0 and game over; with it $FF94 stayed 2 through repeated deaths. GameShark (held every frame): US and JP: same bot run; $FF94 dropped to 1 at each death and was put back to 2 the next frame (six deaths, never game over). Mesen 2 (Dynablaster, and Bomberman Collection through its menu; cheat engine): same bytes at $02:417C; random bot in Game B for 4,000 frames: $FF94 stayed 2 through the deaths (2 -> 1 -> 0 without). GameShark 010294FF ($FF94, HRAM) did not hold in Mesen.

effect: Game B's round clock stays at 200
note: Game Genie: $02:6338, high byte of LD A,($C0EF) in the Game B clock ($02:6328) -> $C9, so it reads $C9EF (never written, 0) instead of the time: AND A / RET Z returns before the DEC, and $C0EF is never decremented. BizHawk: US and JP: new Game B, $C0EF every 120 frames: 199,197,195,193,191 without; 200 x5 with ($C9EF = 0). GameShark (held every frame): US and JP: $C0EF stayed 200 over 600 frames. Mesen 2 (Dynablaster, and Bomberman Collection through its menu; cheat engine): Bomberman Collection takes C93-389-E69 unchanged (Game B clock 200 x5; 199 -> 191 without). Dynablaster's bank 2 is shifted 21 bytes, so the operand is at $02:634D: C93-4D9-E69 held the clock at 200 there, while C93-389-E69 does nothing on Dynablaster (199 -> 191). GameShark 01C8EFC0 held 200 on both.

code: VS MODE with a link cable
effect: Two Game Boys play a head-to-head battle: PANEL or POWERFUL MODE, how many battles, then a 2-player arena and the trophy table; without a partner it shows VS.MODE NOT READY
note: VS MODE ($04:4000) turns on the serial interrupt. The side that presses Start first sends $E0 on the internal clock ($04:4744) and expects $EF back ($46C7-$46E9; $FFA0 = 2 marks the master); any other byte goes to VS.MODE NOT READY ($4D4A). The settings go across at $47B4, then each frame the two pads are swapped ($4792 -> $4752; the partner's lands in $FF8C/$FF8D). Played in Mesen with a scripted partner on the serial port: handshake, settings, the READY splash, a 2-player battle and the 1 WIN MATCH results; with no partner the screen shows VS.MODE NOT READY. The camera follows the local player, so the partner is off screen in the arena. Image: the menu, HOW MANY TIMES OF BATTLE?, READY, the arena, and no partner.
